findings.summary: hidden text admitted the exact issue the gate exists to refuse: the three detectors were regexes over the RAW body, so an issue whose rendered body was 'Please fix the thing. It is broken.' PASSED dispatchable on a nine-line HTML comment (reproduced by the orchestrator). Fenced blocks and <details> the same. The source-text-guard class ADR-0070 §1 bans, on this repo's record twice (reviews/c2ab99e005*, reviews/0a2fcf8b4e*) and reviews/README.md's own worked example. Fixed in 05c2ba4: visibleText() strips comments and fences; <details> deliberately kept (folded is not hidden) and pinned.

the empty-criteria branch was wrong on 6 of 6 real issues it fired on (#95 #96 #127 #186 #280 #306) and its message was factually false in each — the sections were prose or blockquotes, not empty. #306, the best-specified issue in the corpus, was refused because text.search() takes the FIRST matching heading while its bulleted section sat under a later one (reproduced). Demanding a bullet was the header's own magic-word anti-pattern one level down. Fixed: any non-heading content satisfies (a), every matching heading is scanned, message corrected. Corpus 4 → 9 dispatchable; #127 now refuses for a true reason (names no surface).

the production entry point had ZERO coverage: the selftest imported admit() only and substituted a hand-written Set for the probes, so repoProbes, main, the gh call, argv parsing and every exit code were executed by nothing — which is what hid M2. Fixed: the selftest drives main() behind a gh PATH shim, the sibling gate's pattern (reproduction-gate.selftest.mjs).

run from any cwd but the repo root the gate refused EVERY issue, each with a false accusation that src/engine.ts does not exist — and its only intended consumer (D3/D4's orchestrator) polls from its own directory or a per-issue worktree. Fails closed, hence major not blocking. Fixed: the root comes from the SCRIPT's own location (git -C <scripts/> rev-parse --show-toplevel, realpath'd). A first attempt anchored on cwd was insufficient — verified failing from $HOME — and was corrected before commit.
gh was hardcoded to /opt/homebrew/bin/gh: macOS-only, ENOENT swallowed into a wrong diagnosis, and unshimmable so the sibling's test pattern could not be applied. Fixed: resolve 'gh' through PATH.

a decision that does not exist resolved to a different one: BARE_DECISION accepted \d{3,4} and find() used an unanchored startsWith, so ADR-007 matched ADR-0070 — the gate admitted the issue AND printed a governing document it never cited (reproduced). Fixed by anchoring find() on the full 'ADR-0075-' prefix. Narrowing BARE_DECISION to \d{4} was also tried and REVERTED: its in-place mutation changed nothing (0 FAIL), so it would have been an unpinned guard, and the wider match gives the better refusal.

path traversal escaped the repository: src/../../../../../../etc/passwd satisfied clause (b), so the referent was the whole filesystem rather than 'the repository itself' the header claims (reproduced). Nothing is read, so no disclosure. Fixed: any surface containing a '..' segment is refused with its own message. Round 2 note: the behavioural half of this pin is vacuous — with traversing=[] only the MESSAGE check fails, because the selftest's stub has() rejects the traversing path anyway. Carried as an R2 minor.

the design's headline half contributed nothing to the measured split — badsurf 0 across 38 issues and all governing refusals were 'no citation at all', never 'could not be found'. 100% of the discrimination is structural; the existence probes (the answer to the model-as-judge problem, the reason given for the whole design) have never fired on a real issue. A disclosure gap against the header's own standard. Fixed: stated in the header and the PR body as prospective, not the discriminator.

the PR body misstated its own evidence count twice ('20 cases', '20/20'); the selftest was 35. Corrected, and now 63. NOT fully fixed (round 2): the PR body's closing line still read 'admission selftest 20/20 green', and commit 05c2ba4 says '20 → 63' when the true arc is 35 → 63.
the re-verified breakdown dropped the 9 missing-governing category, reading as if the reason had vanished. Corrected.
GOVERNING was /gi but BARE_DECISION only /g, so 'Per adr-0075.' was refused. Both case-insensitive now, with find() upper-casing.
a surface named in a blob permalink was not seen (surfaces named: none). SURFACE now also matches after /blob/<ref>/; pinned, mutation observed red.
'returned' overstated what the script does — it prints and exits, and D1's FSM is unbuilt. The header had a 'does not check' list and no 'does not do' counterpart; added.
three descriptions of the same ruling (brain text 'decided', entry status 'proposed', PR body 'proposed resolution ... needs a ruling'). PR body now says ruled, citing brain 1652256406c1.
find() shelled out to `ls` once per citation; replaced with readdirSync.

mutations.note: CORRECTED after round 2 (R2-M2): this entry was WRONG. The three fence pins did go red, but for an incidental reason — the `|$` alternative under the /m flag stops the lazy match at the first line break, so the stripper removed the opener and ONE line, and all three pins put the payload on the line immediately after the opener. Insert one filler line and the whole 'stripped' payload survives. Per ADR-0070 §2 a mutation the guard did not catch is a FINDING, not a log entry, so this is recorded as observedRed:false and carried as R2-M2. Zero live harm: scanning all 38 issues for surfaces/decisions present in the raw body but absent from visibleText() returned no rows.
